title: Integrated Budgeting, Procurement, Contracts, and Revenue Recognition Policy
author: Ava Chen
summary: This document defines Redwood Inference's integrated policies for annual budgeting and rolling forecasting, procurement and vendor contracting procedures, and revenue recognition and billing controls. It provides governance, approvals, templates, and day-to-day operational steps to ensure accurate financial planning, compliant contracting, and consistent revrec and billing treatment.
body:
Overview:
This policy consolidates the core financial controls and procedures across budgeting & forecasting, procurement & contracts, and revenue recognition & billing. It is intended for Finance, Legal, Procurement, Product, and Engineering stakeholders involved in financial planning, vendor engagements, and revenue operations.

Scope:
- Applies to all Redwood Inference entities and legal entities unless a regional addendum exists.
- Covers annual budgeting, quarterly rolling forecasts, purchase approvals, contracting standards for suppliers and customers, and recognized revenue / billing practices for hosted, dedicated, and private products.

Governance and Ownership:
- Policy Owner: Finance (Ava Chen, Director of Finance).
- Legal Review: Legal Counsel (Priya Nair).
- Procurement Steward: Procurement Lead (Marcus Lee).
- Revenue Operations: RevOps Manager (Lena Rodriguez).
- Changes to this policy require sign-off from Finance, Legal, and Procurement and must be recorded in the revision history section.

I. Budgeting & Forecasting Process
A. Annual Budget Timeline (high level):
1. Strategic planning and top-down target setting (October).
2. Departmental budgets submitted (November).
3. Consolidation and review cycles (December).
4. Executive review and approval (January).
5. Board submission and approval (February).

B. Rolling Forecasts:
- 12-month rolling forecast updated monthly by Finance with inputs from revenue, product, and engineering.
- Drivers tracked: ARR growth, hosting costs (GPU spend), model licensing costs, personnel, and third-party services.
- Material variance thresholds: >5% monthly variance to forecast requires an owner-led variance explanation and corrective plan.

C. Budget Templates and Required Attachments:
- Each departmental submission must include: headcount plan, vendor commitments >$10k, project-level spend >$50k, and one-page narrative describing key assumptions.
- Template (spreadsheet) location: [Finance Drive]/templates/budget-template-YYYY.xlsx.

D. Ownership and Approvals:
- Department Head certifies submission.
- Finance performs validation and flags risks.
- Final sign-off: CFO for company-wide budgets; SVP Product for product-led investments >$250k.

II. Procurement Procedures
A. Procurement Request and Approval Flow:
1. Raise PR in procurement system with business justification and cost center.
2. Thresholds and required approvals:
   - <$5k: Manager approval.
   - $5k - 30k: Dept Head + Procurement review.
   - $50k - 250k: Dept Head + Procurement + Finance (budget check).
   - >$250k: Dept Head + Procurement + Finance + Legal + Exec sponsor.
3. Procurement will run vendor selection for competitive buys >= $50k (3 bids preferred).

B. Vendor Onboarding Requirements:
- Valid W-9 or local tax form, executed Master Services Agreement (MSA) or standard purchase order (PO), insurance certificate (if required), and payment/routing info.
- Security questionnaire must be completed for vendors with access to customer data or internal systems; handoff to Security & Compliance.

C. Purchase Orders and Commitment Accounting:
- POs are required for all purchases >$5k.
- Finance will record committed spend in the committed expenses ledger upon PO issuance.
- Any amendment that changes total committed spend requires re-approval following thresholds above.

D. Procurement Approval Matrix (ASCII table):
| Amount Range | Approvals Required | Procurement Action | Bids Required |
|--------------|-------------------|--------------------|---------------|
| <$5k         | Manager           | Create PR          | No            |
| $5k - 30k    | Dept Head + Procurement | Create PO/Contract | 1-2 preferred |
| $50k - 250k  | Dept Head + Procurement + Finance | Negotiate MSA/PO | 3 bids preferred |
| >$250k       | Dept Head + Procurement + Finance + Legal + Exec | Exec sponsor sign-off, Legal review | Formal RFP recommended |

III. Contracts & Legal Process
A. Standard Contracting Principles:
- Use template MSAs and SOWs maintained by Legal. Deviations from standard templates require Legal sign-off.
- Limitation of liability, IP terms, data protection, and indemnities are redlines that require Legal approval.

B. Contract Review SLAs:
- Standard MSA review: 5 business days.
- Negotiated SOWs and commercial contracts: 10 business days.
- High-risk contracts (data residency, government customers): 20 business days and escalation to General Counsel.

C. Contract Execution:
- Contracts must be stored in the contract repository (ContractDB) with metadata: counterparty, effective date, term, auto-renewal clause, MSA id, SLA references, payment terms, and responsible Finance owner.
- Counterparty signatures: electronic signatures preferred; manual signatures require scanned copy uploaded.

IV. Revenue Recognition & Billing Policies
A. Revenue Streams Covered:
- Hosted API (usage-based): per-token and per-embedding billing.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): committed monthly/annual charges.
- Private (license/support): upfront platform fee + ongoing support/maintenance.
- Professional services (SOW-based): recognized by milestone or percentage of completion as appropriate.

B. Recognition Principles (aligned to ASC 606 / IFRS 15):
- Identify contract(s) with customer, identify performance obligations, determine transaction price, allocate price to obligations, and recognize as obligations are satisfied.
- Usage-based billing recognized when usage occurs (over service period).
- Annual committed capacity billed monthly and recognized ratably over the contract period unless evidence indicates a different pattern of transfer.
- Upfront fees for license with significant standalone functionality: recognize over the period of benefit; otherwise, if distinct, recognize at point in time.

C. Billing Controls and Invoicing:
- Billing cadence: monthly for usage and consumption, quarterly or annually for pre-paid committed contracts per contract terms.
- Invoice approval: RevOps prepares invoices; Finance reviews high-value adjustments (> $50k) prior to issuance.
- Dispute handling: customers must register disputes within 30 days of invoice date. Credits and adjustments recorded with supporting documentation and routed to Finance and RevOps for approval.

D. Deferred Revenue and Contract Liabilities:
- Payments received in advance recorded as deferred revenue on the balance sheet and amortized to revenue per the recognition schedule.
- Finance maintains a deferred revenue schedule with contract-level granularity for any balance > $25k.

E. Audit & Controls:
- Monthly close: RevOps & Finance reconcile billed revenue to recognized revenue and investigate variances >0.5% of monthly recognized revenue.
- Quarterly internal review: sample of contracts and revenue recognition calculations reviewed by Finance and Legal.

V. Operational Playbooks and Checklists
A. New Vendor Onboarding Checklist (Procurement + Finance):
1. Confirm business need and budget availability.
2. Complete Vendor Security Questionnaire if required.
3. Obtain W-9 / local tax form.
4. Execute MSA or PO and upload to ContractDB.
5. Issue PO and notify Finance for commitment accounting.
6. Add vendor to AP system and schedule payment terms.

B. New Customer Contracting & Billing Onboarding (RevOps + Legal + Finance):
1. Use standard Customer MSA and attach SOW with pricing.
2. Confirm billing cadence and payment method.
3. Configure billing system with contract terms and recognition schedule.
4. Validate sample invoices before first billing run.

VI. Templates and Examples
- Standard MSA template path: [ContractDB]/templates/msa-standard-v3.docx
- Purchase Order template: [Procurement]/po-template.xlsx
- RevRec schedule template: [Finance Drive]/templates/revrec-schedule.xlsx

Appendix A — Key Thresholds and Definitions:
- Material variance threshold (forecast): 5% monthly.
- Significant contract amount: >$250k.
- PO requirement threshold: >$5k.
- Deferred revenue review threshold: >$25k.

Revision History:
- 2024-10-15: Document created (Ava Chen).
- 2024-12-12: Procurement thresholds updated (Marcus Lee).
- 2025-02-10: RevRec control clarifications and SLA updates (Finance & Legal).

Contacts and Escalations:

- Procurement: procurement@redwood.ai (Marcus Lee).
- Legal: legal@redwood.ai (Priya Nair).
- RevOps / Billing: revops@redwood.ai (Lena Rodriguez).

Notes and References:

- Accounting guidance: ASC 606 summary (finance drive).

End of policy.
